missing.item: Resolve whether the registration invariant applies when slashing is requested or when it is finalized.
missing.why: The code and reproduction show that a slash requested while the operator is registered can execute after unregistration. The stated allowance to slash pre-unstake conduct leaves unclear whether that sequence violates contest policy.
missing.resolves_when: An applicable contest-policy clause or sponsor statement specifies whether registration is required at request time or finalization time.

missing.item: Clarify whether the post-unregistration depositor’s loss is a distinct impact beyond the queued slash reducing vault assets.
missing.why: The reproduction demonstrates the depositor’s redeemable value falls from 1000 to 950, but the vault asset reduction is also the ordinary result of executing the queued slash.
missing.resolves_when: Explain why the depositor’s dilution is a distinct consequence relevant to the claimed impact, or rely on the invariant violation without that additional impact.

reason: The cited code and passing reproduction support the post-unregistration finalization path and conditional financial loss. Whether this violates the stated invariant remains unresolved; the policy distinction is necessary to establish the claim.

evidence.claim: A DSS can finalize a slashing on an operator after the operator has fully unstaked and unregistered from that DSS, because finalizeSlashing does not re-check registration, breaking the invariant 'Only DSSs an operator is registered with can slash said operator'.
evidence.support_reason: requestSlashing (Core.sol:220-231) checks registration via checkIfOperatorIsRegInRegDSS (Operator.sol:143-148) and stores the queued slashing root (SlasherLib.sol:110). finalizeSlashing (Core.sol:248-256 -> SlasherLib.sol:126-151) only checks the stored root and the veto window; it never re-checks that the operator is still registered to the DSS. unregisterOperatorFromDSS (Core.sol:113-124 -> Operator.sol:181-203) only requires that no vaults remain staked to the DSS (Operator.sol:190), not that no slashing is pending. So a slash queued while registered can be finalized after unregistration.
preconditions: Operator has vaults staked to a DSS and initiates unstake (9-day MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY).
DSS calls requestSlashing while operator still registered and vaults still staked (within the 9-day window).
Operator finalizes unstake and unregisters from DSS before the 2-day SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW elapses.
Anyone calls finalizeSlashing after the veto window.

missing_evidence.item: Whether the invariant 'Only DSSs an operator is registered with can slash said operator' is intended to bind at finalization time or only at request time.
missing_evidence.why: The README also states a DSS can slash conduct that occurred before unstake initiation for up to 7 days, and the SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW is 2 days. A judge could read a slash requested while registered as satisfying the invariant, making the finalization-after-unregistration behavior intended rather than a bug. The report itself concedes this is a design-intent question. Without resolving it, the claim cannot be accepted as a violation.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A contest policy clause or sponsor statement specifies whether the registration invariant is evaluated at requestSlashing or at finalizeSlashing.

missing_evidence.item: Whether the 'new staker loses funds' impact is a distinct harm or merely the intended slashing of the vault's assets.
missing_evidence.why: The vault's totalAssets reduction is the normal effect of a valid queued slash; the report's added harm is that a post-unregistration depositor is diluted. That is a consequence of the same root cause and does not change whether the invariant is broken, so its absence does not undermine the core claim.
